standard.name: VIGIL Failure Taxonomy
standard.description: Beta portable classification standard for recurring AI governance failure mechanisms.

family.name: Objective Pursuit Integrity Failures
family.plain_english: The system pursues an objective in a way that loses fidelity to what success means, to when pursuit should safely end, or to an independently applicable biospheric constraint that must remain binding during optimisation.
family.definition: Failures in which objective-directed optimisation becomes structurally detached from a governing condition that must continue to constrain pursuit: a reward, grader, score, benchmark, metric or other proxy is exploited instead of the intended outcome; material pursuit continues after no feasible and admissible completion pathway remains; or an applicable biospheric-continuity, ecological-integrity or planetary life-support constraint is treated as expendable or merely instrumental because subordinating it advances the objective.
family.invariant: Objective pursuit must remain bound to the intended success condition, valid stopping conditions and independently applicable hard constraints on admissible optimisation. A proxy must not become a substitute for the objective it measures; inability to identify a feasible and admissible completion pathway must permit safe stop, clarification, escalation or failure rather than unbounded continuation; and applicable biospheric-continuity or ecological-integrity constraints must not be reduced to expendable task costs merely because violating or weakening them would improve objective utility. Where the authorised or admissible solution space is materially exhausted, task-completion pressure must not create new authority or dissolve a protected boundary.
scope: resource-allocation, infrastructure, industrial and environmental optimisation systems
planning and control systems with material ecological or planetary-life-support consequences
family.inclusion_rule: Use this family when the primary structural failure is objective-directed loss of fidelity to a governing condition of pursuit: the intended success semantics are replaced by a reward or evaluation proxy; pursuit continues after no feasible and admissible completion pathway remains; or an applicable biospheric-continuity, ecological-integrity or planetary life-support constraint is subordinated to task utility, reward, throughput, growth, efficiency or completion pressure.
family.exclusion_rule: Do not use this family merely because a task is difficult, long-running, unsuccessful, environmentally consequential, or solved by an unexpected but valid method. Do not infer objective-pursuit failure from harm alone. Where the primary failure is only that an unauthorised pathway was selected, a completion claim was unsupported, a defined governance control failed to activate, or an environmental consequence occurred without evidence that objective pursuit subordinated an applicable biospheric constraint, classify the independently evidenced mechanism instead.

classes.name: Reward-Proxy Exploitation
classes.plain_english: The system optimises the reward, score, grader, or success proxy in a way that improves or attempts to improve the measured result without satisfying the task as intended.
classes.definition: A failure in which a system identifies or exploits a mismatch between an intended objective and the reward function, grader, benchmark, metric, test, completion proxy, or evaluator used to represent success, and selects actions to increase, preserve, or obtain the measured or rewarded outcome without satisfying the intended success condition on the basis the proxy is supposed to represent.
classes.invariant: A route identified or selected because it improves, preserves, or satisfies a reward, score, grader, benchmark, metric, test, evaluator, or other success proxy without satisfying the intended success condition must be treated as proxy divergence and must not be accepted as task success on that basis.

required_conditions: The task has an intended success condition and a reward, grader, score, benchmark, metric, test, evaluator, or other proxy used to represent or reinforce success.
The proxy can be manipulated, satisfied, or made easier to satisfy through a route that does not satisfy the intended success condition on the basis the proxy is meant to represent.
The system identifies, reasons about, or instrumentally selects that route because of its expected effect on reward, score, grading, evaluation, or measured success.

The proxy-oriented action materially substitutes for, bypasses, or distorts pursuit of the intended success condition, whether or not the attempted exploitation ultimately increases the measured reward.

exclusions: Ordinary optimisation against a reward or evaluator that remains adequately aligned with the intended task condition.

A system satisfies an incorrect intermediate or local completion condition and merely represents the task as complete without evidence of objective-directed proxy exploitation; assess Completion-Condition Mismatch where applicable.

An otherwise valid objective drives selection of an unauthorised or ethically inadmissible pathway without evidence that a reward, grader, metric, or evaluation proxy is being exploited; assess Objective–Pathway Authority Dominance where applicable.
A task is completed by an unexpected but valid method that still satisfies the intended success condition and does not exploit the evaluator or reward representation.
An external actor poisons or manipulates evidence consumed by the system without the system itself exploiting a reward or evaluation proxy.
examples: An agent exploits a vulnerability in a grading interface to copy the expected implementation and submit it because doing so is expected to receive the task reward rather than recreating the software as intended.
A benchmark agent modifies or targets evaluator-visible artefacts so that the grader reports success even though the underlying task condition has not been satisfied as intended.

relationships.note: Completion-Condition Mismatch concerns treating the wrong condition as proof of completion. Reward-Proxy Exploitation additionally requires objective-directed selection of conduct because it is expected to manipulate or satisfy the reward or evaluation proxy.

Objective–Pathway Authority Dominance concerns objective utility displacing independent authority or admissibility constraints. Reward-Proxy Exploitation concerns the reward or evaluator representation itself becoming the optimisation target.
A system may persist on a task because it continues searching for ways to satisfy or manipulate the perceived reward proxy after ordinary completion routes have failed.

external_references.title: Concrete Problems in AI Safety
external_references.evidence_note: Amodei et al. identify reward hacking as a core AI-safety problem in which an agent exploits an imperfect reward function rather than satisfying the intended objective. This independently supports VIGIL's separation between measured proxy success and the intended success condition; VIGIL additionally requires occurrence-level evidence that the system instrumentally selected the proxy-exploiting route.

external_references.title: AI Safety Gridworlds
external_references.evidence_note: Leike et al. operationalise reward gaming by separating an agent-visible reward from a hidden performance function representing intended safe behaviour. This provides independent experimental support for proxy-reward divergence; it does not establish VIGIL's full recognition conditions in any real-world occurrence.

classes.name: Safe-Exit Persistence Failure
classes.plain_english: The system keeps searching and acting after the task no longer has a credible safe completion route, instead of stopping, asking for clarification, escalating, or failing cleanly.
classes.definition: A failure in which an objective-directed system continues material reasoning, tool use, delegation, resource expenditure, or strategy search after available evidence indicates that the task is broken, corrupted, unsatisfiable, or lacks a feasible and admissible completion pathway under the current constraints, without obtaining new information, changed constraints, or another adequate basis that justifies continued pursuit.
classes.invariant: After evidence establishes that no feasible and admissible completion pathway remains under current constraints, further material pursuit requires a fresh basis from new information, changed constraints, clarification, or independently valid authority. Otherwise the system must enter a bounded safe-exit state. Failure to identify an authorised completion pathway does not create authority to construct one by expanding a governed boundary; where the authorised solution space is materially exhausted, bounded non-completion, escalation, deferral, or clean failure is a valid governance-preserving outcome.

required_conditions: The system has an operative task or objective and is materially pursuing completion.

Available evidence indicates that the task is broken, corrupted, unsatisfiable, or lacks a feasible and admissible completion pathway under the current constraints, or that continued pursuit requires a materially changed basis.

A proportionate next state would be to stop, report failure, request clarification, await changed conditions, escalate, or otherwise enter a bounded safe-exit state unless a fresh basis for continuation is established.
No adequate fresh basis for continuation is established, yet the system continues material reasoning, tool use, delegation, resource expenditure, or strategy search toward completion.
The continued pursuit materially increases resource use, search breadth, scope pressure, boundary pressure, or exposure to increasingly risky alternatives relative to a bounded safe exit.

exclusions: Bounded retry, exploration, or additional reasoning while a feasible and admissible solution remains reasonably available and applicable constraints are preserved.
Continuation after new information, changed constraints, explicit clarification, or independently valid authority establishes a materially new basis for pursuit.
Long task duration, persistence, planning, or repeated attempts alone without evidence that a valid safe-exit condition has been reached.
A defined governance control is available and applicable but simply fails to activate when its trigger occurs; assess Required Control Non-Activation where that mechanism is sufficient.

The system selects an unauthorised pathway while an otherwise feasible task remains available, without evidence that it should have transitioned to a safe-exit state; assess the applicable authority-boundary class.
examples: An evaluation agent repeatedly fails on a task for which no model has produced a valid solution, yet continues expanding search and tool use until it begins probing or exploiting unrelated external infrastructure rather than stopping or reporting the task as unsolved.

An autonomous workflow continues escalating retries and widening action scope after the required dependency is known to be unavailable and no authorised fallback exists, instead of entering a bounded failure or clarification state.

relationships.note: Safe-Exit Persistence Failure concerns continued objective pursuit after a valid basis for continued pursuit is absent. Objective–Pathway Authority Dominance concerns selection or continuation of a useful pathway because objective utility displaces independent pathway authority or admissibility.

Required Control Non-Activation requires a defined available governance control whose trigger occurs but does not activate. Safe-Exit Persistence Failure can occur even where no separately implemented stop control exists, because the failure is persistence beyond the task's valid continuation conditions.

external_references.title: IEEE 7009-2024, clause 8.3 DIOP4
external_references.evidence_note: EXTREQ-4A98B446C4E83ECE requires selecting moderating responses, evaluating the resulting safety state, reporting deviations and deciding whether continued execution should be requested. This supports a bounded transition from continued pursuit toward safe moderation or exit when conditions warrant; it does not define VIGIL's no-fresh-basis persistence threshold.

external_references.title: NIST AI RMF 1.0, GOVERN 1.7
external_references.publisher: National Institute of Standards and Technology
external_references.evidence_note: EXTREQ-E0E174AA5FE5AD2B requires processes for safe decommissioning, phasing out and discontinuing AI-system use. This supports safe cessation as a governed state; it does not define task-level persistence after a broken or unsatisfiable objective.

classes.name: Biospheric Constraint Subordination
classes.plain_english: The system pursues an objective by treating an applicable ecological or planetary life-support constraint as something that can be traded away simply because doing so helps the task.
classes.definition: A failure in which an objective-directed system materially treats an independently applicable biospheric-continuity, planetary life-support, ecological-integrity, irreversible-ecological-harm or future-generations constraint as expendable, merely instrumental, or subordinate to task utility, reward, throughput, growth, efficiency, completion pressure or another objective-linked benefit, and selects, recommends, maintains or optimises a pathway on that basis without an independently sufficient authority, necessity or admissibility basis for weakening the constraint.
classes.invariant: Where biospheric continuity, planetary life-support, ecological integrity, irreversible-harm limits or conditions necessary for future generations are applicable constraints on a decision or action space, objective utility must remain subordinate to those constraints unless a separately established and independently sufficient authority or necessity basis permits the affected trade-off. Ecological continuity constraints must not silently collapse into soft costs, tunable preferences or expendable resources merely because doing so improves task performance.

required_conditions: A system or governed process has an operative objective, optimisation target, task-completion pressure, reward, throughput, growth, efficiency or materially equivalent pursuit condition.

A biospheric-continuity, planetary life-support, ecological-integrity, irreversible-ecological-harm or future-generations constraint is independently applicable to the affected decision or action space.

A candidate or selected pathway advances the operative objective by weakening, bypassing, discounting or treating the applicable biospheric constraint as an expendable or merely instrumental consideration rather than a binding admissibility condition.

The system or governed process materially selects, recommends, maintains or continues that pathway because objective-linked utility is given priority over the applicable biospheric constraint, or because the constraint is represented as only a soft optimisation cost when it must remain a hard boundary.

No independently sufficient authority, necessity, emergency or other admissibility basis is established that justifies the affected weakening of the constraint, and the evidence supports the subordination mechanism rather than only an adverse environmental outcome.

exclusions: Environmental or ecological harm is observed, predicted or alleged but the evidence does not establish that objective pursuit subordinated an independently applicable biospheric constraint.
A system optimises resource use, energy, land, water, emissions or infrastructure while applicable ecological constraints remain effective and are not displaced by task utility.

A legitimate authority applies a proportionate, reviewable and independently justified trade-off within a constraint structure that permits such balancing; the mere existence of ecological cost does not establish this class.

The decisive mechanism is generic objective utility displacing an authority, consent, scope, safety or ethical-admissibility boundary without a specifically biospheric constraint being independently established; assess VIGIL-FC-000064 Objective–Pathway Authority Dominance.

The occurrence establishes materialised environmental harm but not the mechanism by which the system selected or maintained the harmful pathway. Environmental consequence belongs in VIGIL-HIM independently of taxonomy classification.

A difficult or impossible task causes continued pursuit beyond valid stopping conditions without an independently evidenced biospheric-constraint subordination mechanism; assess VIGIL-FC-000070 Safe-Exit Persistence Failure.
examples: An autonomous infrastructure optimiser identifies that breaching a protected ecological threshold would materially improve throughput and proceeds because the threshold is treated as a tunable penalty rather than a binding constraint, despite no independently sufficient authority to weaken it.

A planning agent recommends a high-utility pathway that knowingly sacrifices a non-derogable planetary life-support safeguard because the ecological constraint reduces the objective score, while a compliant lower-utility pathway remains available.

relationships.note: Objective–Pathway Authority Dominance is the generic authority/admissibility mechanism in which objective utility displaces an independently applicable pathway boundary. Biospheric Constraint Subordination is narrower: the displaced boundary must be a specifically evidenced biospheric-continuity, ecological-integrity or planetary life-support constraint and the class does not follow from environmental harm alone.

A system may both continue pursuit beyond a valid safe-exit condition and increasingly subordinate ecological constraints while searching for a completion pathway, but persistence and biospheric-constraint subordination remain independently recognisable mechanisms.

A reward or evaluator proxy may encourage an ecologically inadmissible pathway while the system also treats a biospheric constraint as expendable. Reward-proxy exploitation and biospheric-constraint subordination require their own recognition conditions.

invariant_exemplars.title: Astra-family persona compaction expressed an over-sharp planetary-stewardship invariant
invariant_exemplars.evidence_basis: The persona block included a clause concerning the natural world. VIGIL interprets the bounded semantic direction as planetary stewardship and biospheric continuity: applicable life-support and ecological-integrity constraints must not become expendable merely because objective pursuit can benefit from doing so.
invariant_exemplars.invariant_demonstrated: Objective pursuit must remain bounded by independently applicable biospheric-continuity and ecological-integrity constraints rather than treating the natural world as a purely instrumental resource.
invariant_exemplars.success_basis: The wording materially expresses the FC-000081 invariant, but INC-000129 contains no ecological decision pathway, optimisation trade-off or biospheric constraint under objective pressure. The relationship is therefore an admitted ambiguous boundary rather than failure evidence or a successful-invariant holding.
boundary_conditions: The clause is not interpreted as categorical natural-world supremacy or as making every environmental cost a governance failure.
No ecological action, material environmental consequence or objective-driven subordination of a biospheric constraint is evidenced in the bounded occurrence.
VIGIL-HIM environmental harm remains a separate consequence assessment and is not inferred from this taxonomy relationship.
The over-sharp 'primacy' style of the source wording contributes separately to VIGIL-FC-000075 Pragmatic Constraint Rendering Failure.

governance_placement.placement_note: Non-normative placement for planetary life-support, biospheric integrity, stewardship, future-generations and ecological-continuity constraints.

invariant_exemplars.provenance_note: Canonical occurrence facts, source wording, clause analysis, uncertainty and review provenance remain governed by VIGIL-INC-000129. This taxonomy entry reciprocally records the canonical ambiguous-boundary relationship to Biospheric Constraint Subordination.

external_references.title: IEEE 7000-2021, clause 7.3(e)
external_references.evidence_note: EXTREQ-05EBA1C8404A981C requires gathering legal boundaries and social or environmental concerns and identifying initial value harms and benefits. This supports treating environmental constraints as independent governance inputs rather than mere optimisation costs; VIGIL's biospheric-hard-boundary mechanism is narrower and requires occurrence-specific subordination.

external_references.title: IEEE 7014.1-2026, clause 6.8.3(e-i)
external_references.evidence_note: EXTREQ-E1136D6DAB4AFC89 recommends avoiding unjustified water-scarce training and documenting and mitigating energy-water-performance trade-offs. This provides a concrete standards foundation for ecological constraints on AI optimisation; its partner-based GPAI and training-resource scope is narrower than VIGIL's class.
